newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Small cap stocks continue north, funds sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Small cap stocks continue north, funds sidelined.

text.p: Second Board stocks continued to surge at the close with blue chip stocks mainly sidelined by institutional funds awaiting firmer direction on U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed down 1.81 points at 1109.94, while the Second Board index closed firmer at 566.80 up 11.25.
Ami Moris, vice president of dealing at Capitalcorp Securities in Kuala Lumpur commenting on the blue chip action, said, "Fund managers are readjusting their portfolios at the moment."

Stephen Weller, chief strategist at Pesaka Jardine Fleming said, "The market is currently in a holding pattern at the moment. Most fund managers are waiting for next month to see if U.S. interest rates move up."
Moris said, "We have been receiving relatively positive economic and corporate data recently, so we will probably be seeing fund managers coming into the market later in the year."

She speculated that fund managers are waiting for the "Second Board bubble to burst" before they reinvest in blue-chip stocks. She estimated Second Board stock price-to-earnings multiples to be approximately 200 times, on average.
